newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX trading volume drops 6.9 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX trading volume drops 6.9 percent in 1996.

text.p: The Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) said on Tuesday total trading volume for 1996 fell 6.9 percent from the previous year to 22,568,545 contracts.
Volume for the fourth quarter rose 18.8 percent to 5,057,474 contracts from the same period in 1995, the exchange said in a statement.

The increase in fourth quarter volume came after negative growth in the first three quarters of 1996 due to a decline in volatility in U.S. and Japanese markets, which pulled down overall volume for the year, it said.
Eurodollar futures were the most actively traded with volume of 8.18 million contracts, closely followed by Euroyen futures with 8.16 million contracts.
Nikkei 225 stock index futures were the third most actively traded with volume of 4.89 million contracts, although this represented a 24.3 percent drop over their 1995 volume.

SIMEX said Euroyen futures posted a 24.6 percent rise in turnover over 1995 despite the overall decline in trading volume after they were added to a Mutual Offset System (MOS) with the Chicago Mercantile Exchange last March.
The MOS, established in 1984 for Eurodollar futures, permits users to transfer their positions between the two exchanges, allowing for extended trading hours and greater flexibility.
In 1995, total trading volume on SIMEX rose about one percent although trading in derivatives fell worldwide.
